sentences.text:
Shri Rajesh Pandit, learned counsel for the respondent
 Order

This appeal by the appellant/claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 12.05.2022 passed by Member, MACT, District Ujjain in Claim Case No.61/2022.
2.
The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability is not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in dispute.

As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of injured claimant, who suffered 21.7% permanent disability for specific organ which has to be calculated 10% of entire body by way of fracture of tibia, fibula and ankle of right leg, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,41,200/- along with interest.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6106 2 MA-3806-2023 in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The learned trial Court has assumed the income of the deceased as Rs.7700/- per month on lower side.
The Tribunal has committed error in granting meager amount under various heads i.e. pain and suffering, loss of income and special diet.
Hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the matter.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contends that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the amount of compensation in the matter which does not call for any Gourav Kadam vs Mohammad Saifull on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58170871/
1 interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, more particularly the age of the claimant, nature of injuries, in the considered opinion of this Court, it is revealed that no amount has been awarded to the claimants for permanent disability wheres the doctor has clearly opined 31.6% disability.
Certainly, no opinion is adverted with regard to permanent disability of whole body, but looking to the injuries of organ and fracture, it can be assumed that the injured has 10% disability.
Since, the income of the injured is assumed as Rs.7700/- per month +40% future prospects should be added and multiplier of 18 should be applied with 10% of disability.
Based on the objections, the amount under the different heads to the tune of Rs.27,215/- is reduced to found figure of Rs.25000/-.

Therefore, the amount of compensation deserves to be enhanced and the same is enhanced as under:_ NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6106 3 MA-3806-2023 Heads Amount (Awarded by Tribunal) Enhanced by this Court =Rs.1,41,200 permanent Disability NIL Rs.2,32,848/- (7700+40%x12x18x10%)

(The Tribunal has awarded total Rs.27,215/-
 under the heads i.e. Special Diet,
 attendant and Transportation,
 but the same should be  under these different heads) 
 Medical Expenses : Rs.67,785/- 
 Pain and suffering : NIL/- 
 Loss of Income : Rs.46,200/-

MACT Award :Rs.1,41,200/-
 Enhanced amount :Rs.3,96,833-Rs.1,
 =Rs.2,55,633 6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.3,96,833/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.1,41,200/-.

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant are entitled to an additional sum of (Rs.3,96,833/-1,41,200/-) = Rs.2,55,633/- over and above the amount,
which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
7.
In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The claimants are entitled to get total amount of compensation i.e. Rs.1,41,200/- + Rs.2,55,633/- =3,96,833/-/-.
The enhanced amount i.e. Rs.2,55,633/- shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three month s from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6106 4 MA-3806-2023 learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
